title: Adapt provider configuration and request routing for alternate hosted endpoints
before: At first parent ec658223692f901c7456d5baa426e5a8d696dfb7, the command interface accepted only an API key and base URL. Coder.create required those values, assigned them to the provider SDK, and every chat-completion request contained the common model/messages/temperature/stream fields but no deployment_id or engine routing fields. This coupled provider initialization to coder construction and could not express the additional endpoint type, API version, deployment, and engine settings required by alternate hosted interfaces.
after: At merge commit 549a1a76403e309890410f9538bda2fc4f901758, startup accepts optional base, type, version, deployment ID, and engine settings, maps each supplied value to the corresponding provider SDK module attribute, and initializes the API key before constructing the coder. Coder.create no longer owns provider credentials or endpoint configuration. At the request boundary, deployment_id and engine are conditionally copied from SDK module attributes into ChatCompletion.create keyword arguments. Documentation provides command-line and configuration-file examples. Tests were adjusted to the new Coder.create interface, although no provider-specific behavioral test was added and one benchmark call site still uses the removed positional API-key argument.

title: Restore resumed sessions through the canonical persisted runtime route
before: At parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe, the desktop/TUI resume reader extracted provider, base_url, and api_mode only from top-level model_config keys, then fell back to billing_provider. It did not read model_config.gateway_runtime, even though gateway turns persisted their latest actual provider route there and CLI resume already consumed it through SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime. Consequently, a session whose provider changed through the messaging gateway could resume with its current stored model combined with a stale first-call billing provider or stale top-level route. The shared reader also returned any nonempty top-level route before consulting billing_provider, so delegating to it without adjustment would lose the established fallback that fills a missing top-level provider.
after: At 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480, the desktop/TUI resume reader delegates provider, base_url, and api_mode recovery to SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime. That canonical reader prioritizes a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime, then top-level route fields, and uses a routable billing_provider only to fill a missing provider without overwriting explicit top-level data. CLI and desktop/TUI resume therefore interpret persisted route precedence consistently while retaining bare-billing-bucket filtering and legacy fallback behavior.
diff: The change removes the desktop/TUI reader's duplicated top-level-field and billing-provider resolution, replacing it with a call to the shared session route reader. The shared reader changes billing fallback from a separate last-choice return into setdefault on the accumulated top-level route, preserving top-level endpoint/interface fields while filling only a missing provider. Two regression tests cover a nested latest route conflicting respectively with a frozen billing provider and stale top-level route fields. The focused test file passes 4/4 at the implementation ref; when the two new tests are copied to the parent, those two fail with stale 'anthropic' routing while the two pre-existing cases pass.

title: Adapt outbound reasoning fields to a strict OpenAI-compatible endpoint
before: At parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a, provider selection had no endpoint-specific branch for api.fireworks.ai, so those configurations fell through to the default OpenAI-compatible provider. For any request whose model name contained "qwen3", that provider copied a non-empty assistant message reasoning_content value into reasoning. Replayed thinking history was therefore sent with both fields, although the target endpoint accepted reasoning_content and rejected reasoning as an extra input, causing HTTP 400 failures on multi-turn and tool-call continuations.
after: At 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a, configurations whose parsed hostname is api.fireworks.ai or a true subdomain select a dedicated provider. After applying normal default-provider transformations, that provider creates an outbound message array that removes reasoning only when it is a string exactly equal to reasoning_content on an assistant message. It preserves reasoning_content, distinct caller-supplied reasoning values, source conversation history, and existing behavior for other endpoints.
diff: The change adds and exports a dedicated OpenAI-compatible provider, inserts hostname-based provider routing before the default fallback, and overrides request construction to reverse only the default provider's recognizable reasoning mirror at the outbound boundary. It also adds focused routing and field-preservation tests plus an HTTP integration test that exercises conversion of replayed thought history through provider request construction to a strict endpoint stand-in. Four files changed with 407 insertions.

episode.title: Adapt outbound reasoning fields to a strict OpenAI-compatible endpoint
episode.before: At parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a, provider selection had no endpoint-specific branch for api.fireworks.ai, so those configurations fell through to the default OpenAI-compatible provider. For any request whose model name contained "qwen3", that provider copied a non-empty assistant message reasoning_content value into reasoning. Replayed thinking history was therefore sent with both fields, although the target endpoint accepted reasoning_content and rejected reasoning as an extra input, causing HTTP 400 failures on multi-turn and tool-call continuations.
episode.after: At 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a, configurations whose parsed hostname is api.fireworks.ai or a true subdomain select a dedicated provider. After applying normal default-provider transformations, that provider creates an outbound message array that removes reasoning only when it is a string exactly equal to reasoning_content on an assistant message. It preserves reasoning_content, distinct caller-supplied reasoning values, source conversation history, and existing behavior for other endpoints.
episode.diff: The change adds and exports a dedicated OpenAI-compatible provider, inserts hostname-based provider routing before the default fallback, and overrides request construction to reverse only the default provider's recognizable reasoning mirror at the outbound boundary. It also adds focused routing and field-preservation tests plus an HTTP integration test that exercises conversion of replayed thought history through provider request construction to a strict endpoint stand-in. Four files changed with 407 insertions.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 3ba01990 resolves issue #11657 through PR #11701 and records parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a, four changed files, and the failure mechanism: the endpoint rejects messages[N].reasoning while accepting reasoning_content.

In the parent state, the default provider recognized model names containing qwen3 and mapped assistant messages through mirrorReasoningContentToReasoning, which copied a non-empty reasoning_content string into reasoning when reasoning was not already a string.
The provider selector gained a branch before the default fallback that constructs the dedicated provider when its endpoint predicate matches.

Endpoint recognition parses baseUrl, lowercases the URL hostname, accepts the exact canonical hostname or dot-delimited subdomains, and returns false for absent or malformed URLs; it deliberately does not route by model name.
The endpoint-specific provider first invokes default request construction, then maps the resulting messages through an unmirroring operation without modifying the input request object.

Unmirroring applies only to assistant messages and removes reasoning only when it is a string equal to reasoning_content; non-assistant messages, unequal values, and non-string values are returned unchanged.
The request pipeline invokes provider.buildRequest after constructing the base request and before request capture and SDK execution, making the provider hook an outbound wire-shape boundary.

Conversation conversion serializes model thought parts into assistant reasoning_content before provider request construction, establishing how replayed thinking history reaches the mirroring and unmirroring logic.

Focused tests verify removal of the mirrored field while preserving reasoning_content and source history, recognition of a legitimate subdomain, rejection of a hostile suffix hostname, preservation of a distinct explicit reasoning value, and unchanged mirroring for a non-matching endpoint.

An HTTP strict-endpoint stand-in rejects any assistant reasoning field with a 400-shaped response; the end-to-end test sends an initial turn and a replayed-thinking continuation through the real generator/converter/provider path, receives successful responses, and asserts that reasoning_content but not reasoning reached the wire.
The new provider is exported from the provider barrel and the public openaiContentGenerator module, making it available to the selector and direct construction used by integration tests.

title: Adapt content-generation client configuration to provider-specific endpoint overrides
before: At parent c5ad0abb5de461416306a516ddbb26dc78f87d40, the content-generator adapter only copied an explicitly supplied config.baseUrl into SDK httpOptions, did not consult GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL or GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL, did not validate custom endpoint URLs, and forwarded config.vertexai unchanged; consequently provider mode could remain undefined when the selected authentication type identified Vertex AI but credentials had not populated the flag.
after: At cb289e0724b46ce867b6d3fe4bd0ac6ed890dc45, the adapter gives an explicit baseUrl precedence, otherwise selects the endpoint environment variable associated with the authentication type, validates every selected custom URL as parseable and HTTPS except for loopback hosts, passes the resolved URL through SDK httpOptions, and infers the SDK vertexai flag from the selected authentication type when no explicit flag is present.
diff: The implementation adds a custom-base-URL validator, provider-aware environment fallback and explicit-over-environment precedence, plus authentication-type fallback for the SDK provider-mode flag. Seven focused tests cover both provider endpoint variables, provider selection without inferred credentials, precedence, loopback HTTP, malformed URLs, and insecure remote HTTP; existing API-key expectations are updated from an undefined provider flag to false. Configuration documentation adds the two endpoint variables and their security constraints.

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation constructed httpOptions with config.baseUrl only when explicitly present and passed config.vertexai directly to GoogleGenAI; it contained no custom endpoint validation or provider-specific endpoint environment lookup.
evidence_units.source: git show c5ad0abb5de461416306a516ddbb26dc78f87d40:packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.ts, ContentGeneratorConfig and createContentGenerator SDK-construction branch

evidence_units.claim: The changed implementation parses custom endpoint URLs and rejects non-HTTPS remote endpoints while permitting localhost, 127.0.0.1, and [::1].

The SDK adapter first uses config.baseUrl; only when it is absent does it select GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL for Vertex authentication or GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL otherwise, and it validates whichever custom URL is selected.
The resolved endpoint is assigned to httpOptions.baseUrl and supplied to the GoogleGenAI constructor used for API-key, Vertex, and gateway content generation.
When config.vertexai is absent, the adapter now derives the SDK vertexai option from whether authType is USE_VERTEX_AI.

Unit tests assert that the API-key endpoint environment variable reaches SDK httpOptions with vertexai false and that the Vertex endpoint environment variable reaches SDK httpOptions with vertexai true.
A unit test supplies both endpoint variables with Vertex authentication but no inferred Vertex credentials and asserts selection of the Vertex endpoint and vertexai true.
A unit test asserts that an explicitly supplied endpoint takes precedence over the API-key provider's endpoint environment variable.
Unit tests assert that loopback HTTP is accepted, an unparseable custom endpoint is rejected, and remote HTTP is rejected.
Existing API-key client-construction expectations were changed from vertexai undefined to vertexai false, matching authentication-derived provider-mode behavior.
The configuration reference documents both endpoint override variables, their authentication scopes, and the HTTPS-with-loopback-exception rule.

candidate_atomics.name: resolve-provider-specific-endpoint-override
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve a custom service endpoint with explicit configuration taking precedence over the environment variable associated with the selected provider interface, then propagate it into the downstream client options.

semantic_action.intent: Honor endpoint overrides without routing one provider mode through another provider's endpoint or overriding an explicit caller choice.
semantic_action.pre_state: The downstream client accepts an optional endpoint, but the adapter only forwards an explicit endpoint and ignores provider-specific environment overrides.
semantic_action.post_state: The downstream client receives the explicit endpoint when present; otherwise it receives the endpoint override associated with the selected authentication/provider mode.
semantic_action.validation: Constructor-focused tests assert both provider branches, correct selection when both environment variables exist, and explicit-over-environment precedence.

candidate_atomics.name: guard-custom-endpoint-transport
candidate_atomics.description: Validate custom endpoints before client construction, requiring a parseable URL and secure transport except for explicitly allowed loopback development hosts.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent malformed or insecure remote endpoint overrides while preserving local development and proxy use.
semantic_action.pre_state: Custom endpoints can reach the provider SDK without syntax or transport-policy validation.
semantic_action.post_state: Malformed URLs and non-HTTPS remote URLs fail before client construction, while HTTPS endpoints and HTTP loopback endpoints remain admissible.
semantic_action.validation: Negative unit tests assert the malformed-URL and insecure-remote errors, and a positive unit test asserts that loopback HTTP reaches downstream options.

candidate_atomics.name: align-downstream-provider-mode-with-authentication
candidate_atomics.description: Derive the downstream SDK's provider-mode option from the selected authentication type when credential inference has not already set it.

semantic_action.intent: Keep downstream provider behavior aligned with the explicitly selected authentication interface even when credential discovery leaves the provider flag unset.
semantic_action.pre_state: The selected authentication type may identify the cloud-provider interface while the optional downstream provider flag remains undefined.
semantic_action.post_state: An explicit provider flag remains authoritative; otherwise the downstream flag is true exactly for the cloud-provider authentication type and false for other admitted types.
semantic_action.validation: The no-inferred-credentials test asserts cloud-provider mode is still true, while updated API-key tests assert false rather than undefined.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt-provider-client-to-secure-endpoint-overrides
candidate_workflows.description: Extend a provider client boundary so endpoint overrides are selected according to provider mode, respect explicit configuration, pass a transport safety policy, and remain consistent with the downstream SDK's provider-mode switch.

workflow_graph.goal: Construct the downstream provider client with the correct provider mode and a secure endpoint selected from explicit configuration or the matching provider-specific environment override.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A client adapter supports an explicit endpoint and multiple authentication/provider modes, but environment endpoint controls are ignored, endpoint safety is unchecked, and the downstream provider flag can be undefined.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Provider mode is deterministic, endpoint precedence and provider scoping are deterministic, and any selected custom endpoint is validated before being passed to the downstream client.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence establishes the adapter's intended unit-test oracle but does not include CI status or an independently executed test result.
Behavior for custom endpoint variables under gateway authentication is not directly tested; the implementation's non-Vertex branch would consult the API-key-provider variable.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub evidence bundle omits the PR body, reviews, comments, and status checks, so motivation and CI outcome beyond the code, commit, and tests are unavailable.
Tests were inspected but not executed because the supplied checkout worktree has its tracked files removed; no validation-pass claim is made.
